newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 28.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Thai paratroopers and Burmese forces have clashed briefly near the Thai border village of Pu Nam Rawn where over 2,300 Karen refugees are taking refuge from a Burmese military offensive against Karen rebels. Meanwhile, The United States and Amnesty International are pressing Thailand not to forcibly return Karen refugees fleeing war zones in Burma. (THE NATION) (BANGKOK POST)

- The police and the Bank of Thailand are responsible for the blunder which resulted in three prominent suspects in Bangkok Bank of Commerce (BBC) scam being able to escape trial for allegedly violating central bank orders. Public presecutors say that their Swiss counterparts have promised to send bank documents to Bangkok to back up the Thai legal crusade against Rakesh Saxena, a key suspect in the BBC scandal. ((BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- People in government service will have to resign before they can join the Senate under a proposal agreed by the Constitution Drafting Committee. The panel believes the stipulation will cause officials to put their careers and welfare benefits before any ambitions to enter the Upper House. (BANGKOK POST)

- The private sector has pledged its support for government efforts to boost the economy, saying it is willing to make sacrifices in the short term for longer term gains. The joint standing committee on commerce, industry and banking, which met for the first time since being formed by the Chavalit Yongchaiyudh administration, has issued a communique appealing to all state bodies to work together to manage the economic effectively. (BANGKOK POST)

- The finance and securities industry, the scene of a job bonanza over several years of rapid economic growth, is shedding staff quickly, with several companies having launched voluntary and non-voluntary layoff programs to cope with the dim business prospects of an economic slowdown. (THE NATION)
